messages:
elena: Hey team — hitting a bunch of 502/504s from our production app starting ~09:10 UTC. Clients see `TLS handshake timeout` and `upstream connect error` in the gateway. This started right after the cert rotation window AFAIK. Request sample: `curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...'` -> fails with TLS handshake error. Can we confirm if a cert rolled during that window and whether any resolvers changed?

samir: Thanks for the report — I'm looking at the logs now. Do you have a full curl debug output and an exact timestamp from your side? Any specific regions affected?

elena: Pasted the curl -v output below. Happens from both eu-west and us-west clients. Timestamps: 2026-03-15T09:09:55Z start, multiple retries until 09:15.

elena: ```
*   Trying 13.107.21.45:443...
* Connected to api.redwood.example (13.107.21.45) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* TLS 1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLS handshake timeout
* Closing connection 0
curl: (28) Operation timed out after 30000 milliseconds with 0 bytes received
```

samir: Ok that looks like the client never completed the handshake. I see a cluster-level spike in L7 connection errors around 09:10. Correlating with cert-manager logs... @deploy-bot did we run a cert renewal job around that time?

deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline: cert-rotation-job executed 2026-03-15T09:08:42Z -> ACME OK -> new cert applied to edge-gateway pool (rolling restart)

priya: Rolling restart timing matches. Checking resolver metrics — I see a short burst of DNS NXDOMAIN/servfail from our primary resolver around 09:09:30-09:11:00. TTL was low (60s) for the endpoint so a cache miss could exacerbate.

jules: If the gateway pod restarted while some clients attempted to reuse TCP connections, that can produce handshake failures. Also if SNI was missing or clients pinned an old IP it could hit a node without the new cert.

elena: We don't pin IPs. Our client lib does connection pooling. Any recommended repro steps we can run from our side to confirm?

samir: Quick repro steps: 1) `dig +trace api.redwood.example` to see if DNS answers are consistent. 2) `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example:443 -servername api.redwood.example -tls1_3` and repeat during retry window to see if handshake completes. 3) `curl -v --resolve 'api.redwood.example:443:13.107.21.45' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate` to force a particular backend IP and see behavior.

priya: Also check if your client is using a custom CA bundle or transport that enforces a specific cert fingerprint. During rotation the cert chain may be briefly different (new leaf + old intermediates).

elena: Tried openssl s_client locally, intermittent: sometimes it completes, sometimes times out. `dig +short` returns two IPs, different for two runs.

samir: That aligns with resolver flapping + rolling restarts. When a node with the new cert receives traffic for a connection that was established pre-rotation, the TLS handshake can fail if the socket was half-closed and the client retries to the other IP while the old node is draining.

jules: Action items: 1) Support: collect client tcpdump (pcap) and curl -v output + exact timestamps + endpoints. 2) Eng-infra (priya): check cert rotation rollout strategy and whether we did zero-downtime restart for edge pool. 3) Ops (jules): verify DNS TTLs and resolver health during the window. 4) Customer: if possible, set client to disable aggressive connection reuse temporarily (or reduce keepalive) as a mitigation.

priya: From cert-manager logs: rotation used rolling update with 10s pod grace; seems one or two old pods were removed before the new pods were fully ready due to low readiness probe threshold. I'm going to patch the rollout to increase readiness timeout and add a short pre-stop delay so TLS handshakes don't get interrupted mid-flight.

samir: For immediate mitigation, we can: - extend DNS TTL to 300s to reduce resolver churn - bump readiness to wait for `tls-ready` probe - temporarily enable connection draining on old pods for 60s.

elena: Thanks — we'll do the client-side change today to disable keepalive for a few minutes while you patch. Can you confirm how you'd like us to collect the tcpdump?

samir: Run `sudo tcpdump -i any host api.redwood.example and port 443 -w /tmp/redwood-handshake.pcap` during an occurrence window. Share via the support upload link. Also include your app logs showing retries and request ids.

priya: I'll deploy the patch to the rotation job and roll the edge pool with graceful drain. ETA 30m. I'll post updates here when done.

jules: I'll also open a telemetry alert to detect TLS handshake spikes during cert operations so we can auto-mitigate next time.

elena: Uploaded pcap and curl logs to the ticket (link). Seeing new behavior after your patch — errors dropping ~95% since 09:48.

samir: Great — closing the immediate customer impact loop. We'll follow up with a postmortem describing root cause (race between DNS/resolver flapping + rolling cert restarts + low readiness) and long-term fixes.

priya: Postmortem notes I'll capture: add pre-stop sleep, increase readiness probes, add a cert-rotation-canary stage, and add resolver health gating in rotation pipeline.

elena: Appreciate the quick turnaround. Leaving this thread open until postmortem link posted. :thumbsup:
